hints.S31_A1: He is hunting for ANY MESSAGE ABOUT HIS MISSING BICYCLE, and his eyes sweep the whole NOTICE BOARD. Ask: which verb means to look rapidly across a surface for one piece of information? 'Removed' and 'decorated' change the board, not read it.
hints.S31_A2: The kitten was LOST, alone UNDER THE STAIRCASE, and it stayed there FOR TWO DAYS. Ask: which verb shows a small animal curling up tightly in one spot for warmth and safety? 'Galloped' and 'paraded' would take it away from that spot.
hints.S31_A3: The dash explains the idiom: the search is ALMOST IMPOSSIBLE, because the CROWDED CITY hides the owner among millions. Ask: which idiom means something so tiny and so buried that you can hardly ever spot it? 'Piece of cake' means easy - the opposite.
hints.S31_A4: The dash tells you exactly how the face looked: TIRED, DROOPING AND IN NEED OF CARE, like a WILTED FLOWER. Ask: does that face look sad and abandoned, or fierce, or cheerful? Match the adjective to the wilted flower.
hints.S31_A5: The HONEST girl is giving the wallet up officially, at the NEAREST POLICE STATION. Ask: which phrasal verb means giving something you found over to someone with authority? 'Throw away' and 'run off with' are what a dishonest person would do.
hints.S31_B1: The subject is SOMEONE, not the whole CLASS. Words like someone, everyone and nobody act like ONE person. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb ending in -s?
hints.S31_B2: LAST THURSDAY is finished time, so the verb must be past. Ask: what is the past form of this verb? Careful - it is irregular, so an -ed ending will not work; the vowel itself changes.
hints.S31_B3: A STUDENT FOUND THEM suddenly, cutting across something already going on. Ask: which choice shows an action still in progress at that past moment? A plain past verb would report only a finished job.
hints.S31_B4: The WALLET did not do the action itself - A KIND STUDENT WHO FOUND IT did. Ask: which choice puts the subject on the receiving end, and sets it in the past? Passive = a form of 'be' + the past participle.
hints.S31_B5: Read the statement first: it is negative and it is set in the past ('not where you left it'). Ask: after a negative statement, does the tag turn positive or stay negative? And must the tag keep the tense of the statement?
hints.S31_B6: The statement is positive and it uses HAVE HANDED - a present perfect. Ask: after a positive statement, does the tag flip to negative or stay positive? The tag repeats the same helping verb; it never borrows 'did'.
hints.S31_B7: 'NO TRACE' names one single thing, not many, and THE SEARCH PARTY ARRIVED LAST NIGHT fixes the time in the past. Ask: does a singular subject take a present form, or the past one? 'Were' would need a plural.
hints.S31_B8: TOLD STUDENTS = a reported instruction. Ask: after 'told + person', which form comes next - the plain verb, the -ing form, or the infinitive with its little marker in front? 'Written' is a past participle and cannot follow.
hints.S31_C1: Look at the subject of blank 1: STUDENTS - more than one - and EVERY WEEK signals a habit. Ask: in the simple present, does a plural subject take the plain verb, or the one ending in -s?
hints.S31_C2: The subject here is OUR SCHOOL SECRETARY - one person - and ALWAYS tells you this happens again and again. Ask: does a singular subject in the present tense take the plain verb, or the one with -s on the end?
hints.S31_C3: YESTERDAY puts this action in finished time, and the verb is irregular. Ask: what does this verb become in the simple past? Adding -ed would give you a word that does not exist in English.
hints.S31_C4: 'SPENT THE WHOLE OF TUESDAY' - after 'spend' plus a stretch of time, English demands one particular form. Ask: which form follows 'spent an hour ___' - the plain verb, the infinitive, or the -ing form?
hints.S31_C5: WHILE means the action had already begun when A BOY WALKED IN, and the subject, THE SECRETARY, is one person. Ask: which past continuous form matches a singular subject?
hints.S31_C6: AT THE SAME MOMENT points back into the same past stretch of time, but now the subject is TWO PRIMARY 3 BOYS. Ask: does the past continuous of a plural subject begin with 'was', or with its plural partner?
hints.S31_C7: THE MOST COMMON ITEM ___ AT SCHOOL: the blank works like 'the best book ___ read'. Ask: which form goes straight after a noun like this - the plain verb, the -ing form, or the infinitive with its marker?
hints.S31_C8: RIGHT NOW tells you the action has not stopped - it goes on as you read. Ask: which form shows something happening at this very moment, and which helping verb matches SITI, one person?
hints.S31_D1: The dash explains the blank: A MIX OF PANIC AND HELPLESSNESS, searching THE SAME DRAWER AGAIN AND AGAIN. Ask: which box word describes someone wildly anxious? 'Cheerful' is the opposite feeling.
hints.S31_D2: 'A CLEAR ___ OF THE LOST ITEM' is followed by a list: ITS COLOUR, ITS SIZE and ANY SPECIAL MARKS. Ask: which box word names an account of what something looks like? It must be a noun, because 'a clear' comes first.
hints.S31_D3: The blank comes after HARD TO, so it must be a plain verb, and the job is telling ONE BLACK SCHOOL BAG FROM ANOTHER apart. Ask: which box word means to see the difference between two similar things?
hints.S31_D4: The examples do the work: JEWELLERY and IMPORTANT DOCUMENTS, and they MUST BE REPORTED AT ONCE. Ask: which box word describes things worth a great deal of money? 'Frantic' describes a person, not a possession.
hints.S31_D5: THE OWNER AND THE ITEM come back together, and RELIEF AND GRATITUDE FOLLOW. The blank sits after 'are finally', so it must be a past participle. Ask: which box word means joined again after being apart?
hints.S31_E1: The underlined word tells us HOW the teacher SEARCHED - and searching is an action. Ask: do we describe an action with an adjective, or with an adverb? Most adverbs of manner take the same two-letter tail.
hints.S31_E2: TWO MOUSES cannot be right: this animal does not take a plain -s. Ask: how do you write more than one goose, or more than one tooth? The word changes shape instead of gaining an ending.
hints.S31_E3: 'HIDE' ends with a silent -e. Ask: when you add -ing, does that -e stay or drop away? Compare: make becomes making, ride becomes riding, slide becomes sliding.
hints.S31_E4: Find the real subject: A PAIR OF HOUSE KEYS AND A MOBILE PHONE - two things joined by 'and'. Ask: does a plural subject take 'was', or its plural partner? Do not match the verb to the nearest noun.
hints.S31_E5: The PARENTS belong to more than one student - the whole class of them. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or only make a plural? Where must the apostrophe sit when the owners are many?
hints.S31_F1: Sentence A is the condition; sentence B is the reward that follows it. Ask: after 'If', does the verb stay in the simple present, or take a future helper? Only ONE half of a conditional sentence looks forward - and it is not the 'If' half.
hints.S31_F2: Both sentences name the PURSE, so mention it once and let the relative pronoun carry the second mention. Ask: after 'which', do you still need the word 'it'? And what punctuation holds the extra fact apart?
